AUDIO-SCRIPT-PILOT-A1-AU-CAFE.md — review

WHAT THE DOCUMENT IS
A pilot narration script for a single A1 "Au café" (ordering a coffee) lesson, authored against the spec in AUDIO-LESSON-SCRIPT-SYSTEM.md. It is meant to be the first "Den" (7-stage guided narrated lesson): warm/recall, focus/vocab, input/story, practice, produce, check, cheat sheet, spoken by the coach "Camille." Markup: plain text = English voice, [FR]...[/FR] = French voice, [pause:4] = interactive pause, [sfx:ding], [dir:...]. Ratio ~70% EN / 30% FR. It weaves in the fr.a1.cafe theme.

VERDICT ON THE SCRIPT ITSELF (in isolation)
Pedagogically the writing is strong and genuinely A1-appropriate: single concrete scenario, a clean I+1 arc (café -> please -> combine -> je voudrais -> l'addition), short FR phrases under 6 words, warm achievable tone, good intra-lesson recycling and a can-do outro. As a piece of instructional copy it is above average and on-brief for CEFR level and motivation. No em dashes (house rule respected). Question marks kept for TTS prosody.

THE PROBLEM IS THE GAP TO CODE
The runtime this script depends on does not exist. Inspected ealch-v2/src/content/{schema.ts, lessons.ts, drills.ts, playlists.ts, wordOfDay.ts, seed.json} and ealch-v2/src/services/{tts.ts, sound.ts, content.ts}. Findings:
- schema.ts has NO narration field (0 occurrences of narration/LessonNarration/NarrationStage). The §7 schema addition was never made.
- There is no parseNarration tokenizer anywhere in the repo. The §5 segment walker does not exist.
- services/tts.ts still hardcodes language: 'fr-FR' and exposes no lang option. The one-line §5 extension (lang?: 'fr-FR' | 'en-US') was not done. Fed to today's player, the ENTIRE script — including every English sentence like "Today we are going somewhere you'll go all the time in France, a cafe" — would be spoken by a French voice at fr-FR. That is a shipping-breaking mismatch, not a polish item.
- The "Den" that actually exists (lessons.ts: sons3, a1_4, a2_1) is a static table + examples + errors + multiple-choice quiz. It is not a 7-stage narrated audio lesson, and there is no café Den lesson wired anywhere (extendedLesson maps only sons-2/a1-3/a2-0). This pilot is currently orphaned content.
- Only ding.wav (and the other 5 cues) exist in sound.ts, so [sfx:ding] would work once a player consumes it — the one piece that is ready.

CONTENT/CORPUS RECONCILIATION
The doc claims its six woven items are "the item IDs the drills already key against." Checked seed.json fr.a1.cafe.*: only bonjour, je voudrais (.003), and l'addition, s'il vous plaît (.004) match as discrete items. There is NO standalone "un café" item, NO standalone "s'il vous plaît" item, and "merci" exists only as "Merci beaucoup" (.002). "un thé" is not in the corpus at all. So most of what the lesson teaches as atoms are not SRS-scheduled items.

RETENTION-CRITICAL
Per the spec §6, the Den narration is explicitly non-graded and schedules zero review cards ("only item-recall drills schedule cards"). So a learner finishes the flagship guided lesson and nothing enters the spaced-repetition queue. Combined with the corpus mismatch above, the vocabulary taught here has no path back to the learner. For a retention product, the marquee lesson type currently produces no memory trace.

Full note-by-note detail, retention impact, and concrete recommendations follow in the notes array.
topic: Narration runtime does not exist (promise vs code)
observation: The pilot is unplayable as designed. schema.ts has no narration/LessonNarration/NarrationStage field (0 occurrences), there is no parseNarration tokenizer anywhere in the repo, and no 7-stage Den player consumes [FR]/[pause]/[sfx] segments. The only existing 'Den' lessons (ealch-v2/src/content/lessons.ts: sons3, a1_4, a2_1) are static table+quiz screens. This script is orphaned content with no code path to render it.
recommendation: Do not treat the pilot as shippable content. Land the §5/§7 infrastructure first, in order: (1) additive narration?: LessonNarration field + hand-rolled validator in schema.ts; (2) pure parseNarration(block): Seg[] with node --test coverage (mirror progress.logic.ts discipline); (3) a Den player that walks segments. Only then does authoring more scripts create value rather than backlog.

doc:
AUDIO-LESSON-SCRIPT-SYSTEM.md — pedagogy & retention review (reviewed against ealch-v2/src/content/{schema,lessons,curriculum,drills,playlists,wordOfDay}.ts, seed.json, services/tts.ts, store/progress.logic.ts, app/{den,lesson}.tsx, and the pilot AUDIO-SCRIPT-PILOT-A1-AU-CAFE.md).

VERDICT: The design is architecturally strong and the pilot script is genuinely well-crafted, but the document systematically overstates how much already exists, and the one thing that most drives this app's retention model — the graded attempt log that feeds the SM-2 SRS, Den progress, and weak-spots — is explicitly left untouched by the flagship narrated lesson.

WHAT IS REAL IN THE CODE. The corpus (seed.json v1) has 17 items across 3 themes (cafe:9, dictee:3, objets:5), 17 units, only 3 wired lessons (sons.03.l1, a1.04.l1, a2.01.l1), and 2 scenarios — both "Au marché" (sc.a1.marche.001, sc.a2.marche.001). A real SM-2 scheduler exists (progress.logic.ts: nextCard/srsCards/dueCards, ease clamped 1.3–3.0, keyed on item attempts). Den progress and weak-spots are honestly derived from correct attempts on item ids. tts.ts works but hardcodes language:'fr-FR' and its speak() signature is (text,{slow,rate,onDone,onError}) — there is NO lang parameter.

WHAT THE DOC CLAIMS EXISTS BUT DOES NOT. (1) "The Den is already warm/recall → focus/vocab → input/story → practice → produce → check → cheat sheet, walked by Camille (guided-autoplay or self-pace)" — false. den.tsx is a unit list with a progress bar; lesson.tsx renders typed LessonSection lists (teach/steps/examples/quiz…). There is no 7-stage narrated player, no Camille walker, no autoplay toggle. (2) The §7 schema addition (narration?: LessonNarration, NarrationStage) is NOT in schema.ts; no lesson in seed.json carries a narration field. (3) parseNarration, the Seg[] parser, the pause UI, per-segment lang switching, and the described validator do not exist anywhere. The whole system is greenfield, not an "extend what's there" integration — the repeated word "already" misrepresents the starting point and will mislead effort estimates.

WHAT THE PILOT PROMISES BUT THE CORPUS LACKS. The §1 locked decision and the pilot both say the A1 café lesson "reuses the existing fr.a1.cafe theme + the café roleplay." The theme exists; the café roleplay does NOT — the only scenarios are marché. There is also no A1 café *lesson/unit* to attach narration to (a1.04 is articles définis). And the pilot's "corpus items woven in" list cites French strings, several of which are not discrete items ("un café" and standalone "s'il vous plaît" are not items; the closest are fr.a1.cafe.003 "Je voudrais…" and .020 "Je voudrais un café s'il vous plaît"), so the "these are the item IDs the drills already key against" claim is inaccurate.

The retention-critical gap and the CEFR ramp are detailed in the notes, most-severe first.
topic: SRS / review-loop fit — narrated lesson is retention-inert
observation: §6 states plainly: 'No scoring here (this is narration, not a graded drill)… only item-recall drills schedule cards.' The entire progress model in this app is driven by the attempt log (progress.logic.ts logAttempt → srsCards/dueCards SM-2, den.tsx 'learned' counts, weak-spots). A learner can complete a full 7-stage guided lesson — repeating, producing, and answering CHECK questions aloud — and their Den unit stays 0/N, no SRS card is created or advanced, and no weak spot is recorded. The flagship experience does not move the very system the app was rebuilt around. 'The produce stage can hand off to an existing mic drill later' defers the only part that would make it count.
recommendation: Make the CHECK and PRODUCE stages real graded micro-recalls that call logAttempt against the recycled item ids. The infrastructure already exists (stt.ts speech-to-text, roleplay/score.ts, logAttempt, srsCards). This respects the §6 guardrail (they ARE recall, not passive exposure) while letting a narrated lesson create and advance SRS cards, fill Den progress, and surface weak spots — turning the Den from a listen-only feature into a retrieval engine.

doc: EXAMINER-ENGINE-SPEC.md — vision spec for a timed mock-exam engine (TEF/TCF/DELF-DALF), the intended premium/exam-tier wedge. Self-described build status: "not built" (today it is 3 static home chips routing to /speak). The pedagogical core is unusually honest and strong: original-items-only for copyright/trademark safety, no-rubric-no-marking, transcript-based speaking marks with pronunciation shown as an honest verdict not a fake %, "indicative simulation not an official score" framing, calibration against native reviewers with stored prompt_version, and feedback-not-just-a-grade. Launch set is Canada/immigration (TEF Canada + TCF Canada + DELF B2), which matches the highest-willingness-to-pay segment. The format reference is detailed and flags its own recency conflicts. The document's weaknesses are (1) it overclaims existing foundations — the "content schema exam hooks (exam_task, roleplay_scenario.exam{})" it lists as reusable do not exist in schema.ts; (2) it presumes upstream content the app does not have — the entire corpus is A1-only, with zero B1-C2 items to support a B2/immigration exam tier; and (3) its review-loop promises ("SRS surfaces exam weak areas") do not fit the scheduler and weak-skill taxonomy actually built. As a retention product it is well-aimed at a paying niche, but the content floor and the mock-to-remediation loop it depends on are both missing in code.
topic: Overclaimed schema foundations (doc vs code)
observation: Spec line 7 lists as already-existing reusable foundations 'the content schema's exam hooks (exam_task payload, roleplay_scenario.exam{})'. Neither exists. schema.ts Scenario is {id, level, theme, title, turns[], version} with no exam{} field, and there is no exam_task type anywhere in ealch-v2. The exam data model in section 2 is entirely greenfield, not an extension of shipped hooks. This misrepresents build readiness and will corrupt sequencing/effort estimates for the premium wedge.
recommendation: Correct the build-status line to state the exam schema is greenfield, or actually add the fields (Scenario.exam{track, section, rubric, model_answer}, an ExamTask type, format_version) to schema.ts with validators, so the claim becomes true before it is planned against.

topic: 'Equated 5-series' claim outruns available difficulty data
observation: Section 4 promises equated parallel forms with per-item difficulty 'tracked from real attempt data and rebalanced', but the attempt log (AttemptEntry) records only score/verdict/correct on atomic items — no p-values, discrimination, or exam-item psychometrics — and a pre-launch app has no attempt volume to equate against. doc: CONTENT-GENERATION-PIPELINE-SPEC.md
topic: Promise vs. reality: the entire pipeline is unbuilt
observation: The spec describes an 8-stage AI-generation-plus-native-review engine producing ~108 themes and exam banks with deterministic gates, LLM-judge, Gate H, batch TTS, and OTA publish. None of Stages 1-6 exist in the codebase. What the app actually ships is a hand-authored seed (ealch-v2/src/content/seed.json): 17 corpus items across 4 themes (cafe, dictee, objets, marche), 3 extended lessons (sons.03.l1, a1.04.l1, a2.01.l1), and 2 role-play scenarios. ealch-admin/scripts contains only port-content.ts / publish-content.ts / seed.ts — porting and shipping existing prototype content, not generating anything. There is no generation runner, no gate stage, no LLM-judge, no distractor_rationale, no idempotency-keyed queue. The doc reads as forward-looking architecture, but nothing labels it as such, and the '~108 themes' framing implies a library that is ~4 themes deep in practice.
recommendation: Mark the spec explicitly as target-state/roadmap and add a 'current state' header stating the real corpus size (4 themes, 17 items, 3 lessons). More importantly, the vertical-slice section (§Prove-it-first) should be promoted to THE immediate task: a learner past the cafe theme runs out of content in one session, which is the single largest retention cliff. Prioritise breadth of real, reviewed A1 content over pipeline sophistication.

doc: CONTENT-GENERATION-PIPELINE-SPEC.md
topic: Provenance and review-lifecycle fields are absent from the content atom
observation: The spec's central principle is 'every item carries provenance end to end: job_id, prompt_version, model, schema_version, generated_at, reviewed_by, status.' The actual Item type in schema.ts has none of these — only id, kind, level, theme, fr, en, ipa?, gender?, example?, notes?, tags, drills, audioRef?, version. CONTENT_STATUSES = ['draft','in_review','published','archived'] is even declared in schema.ts but is never attached to Item, Lesson, or Scenario. So the Gate H workflow, the 'stale by version hash' targeted-regen mechanism, and the content-health feedback loop (Stage 8) have no schema hook to hang on. The whole traceability story is unrepresentable in the shipped data model.
recommendation: If the pipeline is real intent, add a provenance sub-object and a status field to Item/Lesson/Scenario in schema.ts now (optional, so the seed stays valid), and extend validateItem to enforce that published corpus carries reviewed_by + status='published'. Without a status field on the atom, the native-review gate cannot actually gate what reaches a user.

doc: CONTENT-GENERATION-PIPELINE-SPEC.md
topic: SRS: spec targets FSRS-6, code ships SM-2 — and violates its own minimum-information rule
observation: §Cross-cutting says 'target FSRS-6 (~20-30% fewer reviews than SM-2)' and 'generate to minimum-information / one-fact-per-card, select the best ~10-15 sentences per unit.' The actual scheduler in progress.logic.ts is explicitly 'an SM-2-shaped interval' (ease 1.3-3.0, 1->3->interval*ease ladder, day-granular). No FSRS. Separately, SCHEDULABLE includes 'sentence' and 'dictation', so whole sentences (e.g. 'Il a mangé ses croissants avec sa sœur.') and multi-tile sentences become recall cards — directly contradicting the doc's own one-fact-per-card prescription. The SRS engine itself is honest and well-built (derived purely from the attempt log, no second source of truth), but it is a different algorithm than the spec advertises, and card granularity is not governed by any generator post-filter.
recommendation: Either downgrade the doc's claim to 'SM-2 today, FSRS-6 as a later upgrade' (SM-2 is perfectly adequate at this scale and the ~20-30% figure is not a launch-blocker), or actually adopt an FSRS implementation. Regardless, add the promised minimum-information post-filter: sentence/dictation items scheduled as recall cards should be tagged so the SRS spaces the atomic fact (the accent, the gender, the liaison), not the whole sentence.

doc: CONTENT-GENERATION-PIPELINE-SPEC.md
topic: IPA is a Stage-2 deterministic gate in the spec but is 0% populated in the corpus
observation: Stage 1 lists ipa as an emitted slot and Stage 2 makes IPA a deterministic gate (Phonemizer/espeak-ng, treat LLM IPA as a candidate). In the shipped corpus, not a single Item carries an ipa value (grep: 0 of 17). IPA only exists in wordOfDay.ts (the 8 daily words) and inside lesson tables as free-text cells. For a product whose headline pedagogy is pronunciation (the entire 'sons' track, the 'La Voix' playlist), shipping vocabulary with no phonetic transcription and relying solely on device TTS is a real quality gap — TTS mispronounces liaison and nasal edge cases, which is exactly what this app claims to teach.
recommendation: Backfill ipa on at least all 'sons'-track and voiceflash items before adding themes; it is cheap (espeak-ng batch) and directly supports the pronunciation value prop. Do not let the spec's elaborate IPA gate obscure that the current corpus has no IPA at all.

doc: CONTENT-GENERATION-PIPELINE-SPEC.md
topic: Level discipline is unenforced where it matters most: playlists and word-of-day
observation: The Master-Prompt 'LEVEL DISCIPLINE' rules (tense scope, word caps, >=30% recycled vocab, <=8 new items, Token Miss Rate) are set-ops over a taught lexicon — but the app has no taught-lexicon tracking and applies no level gate to two of its most-visible content surfaces. playlists.ts has no level field at all, yet ships Argot ('j'ai un taf de dingue', 'on se capte plus tard') and L'Argent business register ('revenons à l'ordre du jour', 'le trafic est momentanément interrompu') — solid B2/C1 material presented flat to a user who may be on A1 lesson 4. wordOfDay.ts is 8 abstract literary nouns (flânerie, dépaysement, émerveillement, terroir, convivialité) — lovely, but far above A1/A2 and disconnected from anything the learner is being taught or will be quizzed on. A beginner meeting only untaught, over-level words erodes the sense of progress.
recommendation: Add a level (or minLevel) field to Playlist and to DictEntry, and gate/sort by the learner's current level. Keep the advanced playlists as aspirational 'unlockable' content rather than default home cards for A1 users. Tie word-of-day to the learner's active theme/level so the daily word reinforces the curriculum instead of sitting beside it.

doc: CONTENT-GENERATION-PIPELINE-SPEC.md
topic: Distractor quality has no gate and no rationale field — the spec's Stage 3 gap is real in the data
observation: The spec correctly identifies distractor validity as 'the gap constrained decoding cannot catch' and prescribes an adversarial cross-check plus a distractor_rationale slot. Neither exists: quiz questions in lessons.ts/seed.json are just {q, opts, correct} with no rationale, and there is no check that wrong options are unambiguously wrong. Some shipped distractors are weak: 'The article for ALL plural nouns is...' offers les/las/los (las/los are Spanish, trivially eliminable, so the item tests nothing); 'In les-amis the s sounds like... s/silent/z' is fine. Low-effort distractors let learners pass by elimination without knowing the answer, which inflates the SRS's competence estimate and mis-schedules review.
recommendation: Add an optional why/rationale to each quiz option in the LessonSection quiz type and require it in review. Replace cross-language throwaway distractors (las/los) with plausible French near-misses (le/la/les) so the item actually discriminates. This matters more than most pipeline stages because bad distractors corrupt the attempt log the entire SRS is built on.

doc: CONTENT-GENERATION-PIPELINE-SPEC.md
topic: Exam banks and the examiner are promised here but have no corpus representation
observation: The spec repeatedly scopes in 'the exam banks', exam_task entities, format_version, model answers, rubrics, answer keys, and disclaimers (Stages 0,1,5,7). The schema.ts corpus has no exam_task type — only Item, Lesson, Unit, Scenario. There is a separate EXAMINER-ENGINE-SPEC.md, but the shipped Corpus type cannot hold an exam item, and none exist. So the '100% review for all exam model answers + rubrics + answer keys' cost line and the format_version publish gate are describing content the data model can't yet carry.
recommendation: Defer exam-bank language in this pipeline doc until the exam_task schema exists, or cross-reference EXAMINER-ENGINE-SPEC.md as the owner and remove the half-specified exam hooks here. Exam prep is a strong retention/monetization driver later, but claiming it in the generation spec before the schema supports it creates the same promise-vs-reality gap as the rest of the pipeline.

doc: CONTENT-GENERATION-PIPELINE-SPEC.md
topic: No pathway for introducing new material — the review loop can starve or flood
observation: The SRS is honest by design: 'An item the learner has never attempted is not a card; new material is introduced by drills and lessons, not by the review queue.' But there is no engine that paces new-item introduction, interleaves themes, or balances new-vs-due each day. selectItems (content.logic.ts) is a flat filter by drill/level/theme with no progression or interleaving. With only 4 themes of items, a motivated user exhausts new material fast, then faces either an empty due queue (nothing to do) or, after cramming, a flood of same-day due cards. The spec's comprehensible-input and recycling rules would govern this, but they live only in prose about a generator that isn't wired to selection.
recommendation: Independent of the generation pipeline, build a daily-session composer that mixes N due cards + M new items at the learner's level and interleaves themes. This is the concrete mechanism that turns 'content exists' into 'a reason to open the app tomorrow', and it depends on corpus breadth (Note 1) more than on any gate.

doc: CONTENT-GENERATION-PIPELINE-SPEC.md
topic: Minor pedagogical/accuracy nits in the three shipped lessons
observation: The three real lessons are pedagogically sound overall, but: (a) a2.01.l1 renders 'nous parlons' as 'par-lõ' using the Portuguese tilde õ instead of French ɔ̃, inconsistent with the nasal lesson's own notation; (b) the un/um = œ̃ contrast in sons.03.l1 is taught as fully distinct, though modern Parisian French widely merges œ̃ into ɛ̃ — worth a footnote so learners aren't confused when natives don't distinguish it; (c) 'About 90% of French verbs are regular -ER verbs' is a defensible but loose stat stated as fact. These are small, but this is precisely the content a native-review gate (Gate H) is meant to catch, and it currently runs on nothing.
recommendation: Run the existing 3 lessons + 17 items through one real native-reviewer pass now, as the literal first exercise of Gate H, and fix the IPA notation inconsistency and the œ̃/ɛ̃ note. Proving the review gate on the tiny existing corpus de-risks it far more cheaply than specifying it against 108 imaginary themes.

doc: CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md — review against shipped code (ealch-v2/src/content, src/services, src/store/progress.logic.ts)
topic: Document is stale — shipped architecture diverges from every core prompt
observation: The pack (dated 2026-07-13) prescribes: kebab slugs like 'sons-03-voyelles-nasales' (Prompt A); Supabase SQL content tables content_units/content_items/audio_assets/content_releases + RLS (Prompt B); a config.ts-clone ContentService with hand-rolled guards (Prompt C); a scripts/content/ Node runner (Prompt E). What actually shipped is a different, more capable design: dotted immutable ids ('sons.03', 'fr.a1.cafe.001', 'sons.03.l1') in src/content/schema.ts; a Supabase Storage manifest.json + SHA-256-verified snapshot OTA pipeline (src/services/content.ts + content.logic.ts) — NOT SQL content tables; a full Corpus model with referential-integrity validation; and a separate Next.js Ops Console (../ealch-admin) rather than scripts/content/. supabase/ has schema.sql, not the content-schema.sql the doc mandates. The document therefore no longer describes the system and would misdirect anyone executing its prompts.
recommendation: Mark CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md as SUPERSEDED at the top, pointing to schema.ts (canonical content shape) and content.ts/content.logic.ts (load/merge/verify) as the source of truth. Do not run Prompts A/B/C/E as written — they target an architecture that was replaced.

doc: CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md — review against shipped code (ealch-v2/src/content, src/services, src/store/progress.logic.ts)
topic: Content volume is near-empty — the single biggest retention risk
observation: seed.json ships 17 units but only 3 openable lessons (sons.03.l1, a1.04.l1, a2.01.l1), 17 corpus items (all level a1: themes cafe/objets/dictee), and 2 role-play scenarios (3 turns each). curriculum.ts advertises 43 unit rows (9 sons + 26 a1 + 8 a2) in the Den, so ~40 units render as shells with no lesson behind them. Word of the day is 8 entries (repeats every 8 days); playlists are 4 lists of 2-4 tracks. A motivated learner exhausts every piece of real content in a single sitting. The doc's own milestone ('prove the pipe with one bundle', then Wave 1 generation) concedes this, but no generated content has landed.
recommendation: Treat corpus volume as the critical path, above any further plumbing. Target at least the A1 track fully authored (26 units x ~1 lesson + 100+ items) before any launch. Until then the app is a demo; retention cannot be evaluated because there is nothing to retain users with.

doc: CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md — review against shipped code (ealch-v2/src/content, src/services, src/store/progress.logic.ts)
topic: Placement test is still fake theatre — the doc's honesty fix was never applied
observation: Prompt A's footnote task explicitly said to remove the fabricated 'Q7' label, the fixed 58% progress bar, and copy implying multiple adaptive questions. None of that was done. app/placement.tsx still hardcodes the 'Q7' label (line 65), a static width:'58%' fill (line 61), decorative waveform bars, a fake 'adaptive estimate' chip that flips on one answer, a single question, and a hardcoded A2/A1+ result with 'Start at unit 12/8'. It presents itself as a confident adaptive CEFR test while asking exactly one question.
recommendation: Either relabel honestly (single-question 'quick check', drop Q7/58%/'adaptive' language) now, or gate placement behind a real item bank. As shipped it is an App Store 2.3.1 'misleading' rejection risk and erodes trust the moment a tester retakes it and sees identical theatre.

doc: CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md — review against shipped code (ealch-v2/src/content, src/services, src/store/progress.logic.ts)
topic: SRS engine is genuinely strong but starved of fuel
observation: src/store/progress.logic.ts implements a real SM-2-shaped scheduler (applyGrade/srsCards/dueCards) derived purely from an append-only attempt log, day-granular, with honest due counts and weakest-first ranking. This is the correct spaced-repetition backbone and it is pure/testable. But it only schedules items that have actually been attempted, and the corpus is 17 items — so the review loop has almost nothing to circulate. The retention mechanism exists; the content that would make it fire daily does not.
recommendation: Keep the SRS as-is (it is well built). The unlock is corpus volume: the scheduler needs ~100+ attemptable items per active level for daily reviews to feel substantive. Confirm every drill screen actually writes AttemptEntry rows (verify flashcards/dictation/sentence/voiceflash all log), or the log stays empty and dueCards returns nothing regardless of corpus size.

doc: CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md — review against shipped code (ealch-v2/src/content, src/services, src/store/progress.logic.ts)
topic: All audio is device TTS; recorded/verified audio does not exist
observation: src/services/tts.ts uses expo-speech device voice only; the remote-provider branch (line 38) is an empty stub. schema.ts Item.audioRef is documented 'Null until Phase 7'. The sons/pronunciation track teaches nasal vowels, liaison and the French R — precisely the features device TTS renders unreliably. The doc's issue-12 TTS bake-off (Prompt E bakeoff.js) has not run; no provider chosen. So the pronunciation course is taught with the least trustworthy possible audio.
recommendation: Prioritise the TTS bake-off (liaison/number/homophone trap set) and wire the remote-audio path for at least the sons track before promoting pronunciation as a feature. Bad model pronunciation in a pronunciation lesson is actively mis-teaching, not merely low-fi.

doc: CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md — review against shipped code (ealch-v2/src/content, src/services, src/store/progress.logic.ts)
topic: CEFR level labelling: the A2 track front-loads A1 grammar
observation: a2.01 'Verbes réguliers' (lessons.ts a2_1) teaches present-tense regular -er/-ir/-re conjugation and is tagged 'A2 — SURVIE'. Present-tense regular verbs are core CEFR A1 material, not A2. The whole A2 track opens with present-tense verb families and basic prepositions/adjective agreement that CEFR places at A1. The three authored lessons themselves are pedagogically sound (good IPA, real common-error callouts), but the track's CEFR banner over-states level.
recommendation: Rename the A2 track to reflect its true late-A1/A1->A2 transition content, or move present-tense units into A1 and reserve A2 for passe compose, object pronouns and comparatives. Mislabelled levels break the placement promise ('start at the right unit') and disappoint learners who expected A2 and got A1 review.

doc: CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md — review against shipped code (ealch-v2/src/content, src/services, src/store/progress.logic.ts)
topic: The scaled-generation + human-review promise (issue 4) is entirely unfulfilled
observation: The pack's premise is a generation -> machine QA -> adversarial LLM crosscheck -> human 15% sample -> publish pipeline that would produce trustworthy French at volume. In the shipped tree the only French content is 3 hand-authored lessons and ~17 items; there is no evidence any generated corpus has passed QA or human review (Gate H). The generation/QA lives in a separate ealch-admin app, but the corpus it should be filling is still effectively empty. The central bet of the document has not been proven even once.
recommendation: Run the 'prove the pipe with one bundle' milestone end-to-end for a single A1 theme and measure it (schema-valid? typography-clean? human-approved?) before committing to Wave 1. Do not scale generation until one bundle has cleared human review; unreviewed LLM French reaching beginners is the pedagogically toxic outcome the doc itself flags.

doc: CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md — review against shipped code (ealch-v2/src/content, src/services, src/store/progress.logic.ts)
topic: Exam surface is vaporware and the exam disclaimer string was never added
observation: No exam/examiner screen exists (no exam.tsx/examiner.tsx). Prompt B's i18n task to add an 'examDisclaimer' string (not affiliated with France Education international / CCI Paris) to src/i18n/strings.ts was not done — grep finds zero matches. Issue 5 (exam copyright/format_version) is fully open. Exam/DELF-prep is positioned elsewhere as a headline retention and monetization hook, but nothing is built.
recommendation: Either descope exam from near-term retention messaging, or build a minimal honest exam-practice surface. If exam copy is planned, add the affiliation-disclaimer string now (cheap) so it is ready and legal-reviewed before any exam UI ships.

doc: CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md — review against shipped code (ealch-v2/src/content, src/services, src/store/progress.logic.ts)
topic: Document's payload taxonomy does not match the shipped schema
observation: Prompt E lists payload types lesson/card/vf_item/roleplay_scenario/dictation_item/sb_puzzle/speak_drill/episode/review_seed/exam_task/coach_brief and says lesson must match the OLD src/content/lessons.ts type field-for-field. The actual canonical model (schema.ts) is Item/Lesson/Unit/Scenario, where Lesson is an ordered LessonSection[] (teach/steps/examples/useCases/hacks/cheatSheet/commonErrors/focus/table/audio/practice/quiz) and drills are the closed set flashcard/voiceflash/dictation/sentence/roleplay/review. Concepts like sb_puzzle, speak_drill and episode have no schema home. Generating against the doc's taxonomy would yield shapes the app cannot render.
recommendation: Regenerate the JSON-Schema/generation contract from schema.ts (the four-consumer source of truth), not from the doc's payload list. Delete or reconcile the sb_puzzle/speak_drill/episode/coach_brief types before any generation job is written, or QA will pass content the app silently cannot show.

doc: CONTENT-PART4-FIX-PROMPTS.md — review against shipped code (ealch-v2/src/content, src/services, src/store/progress.logic.ts)
topic: Daily-hook surfaces (word of day, playlists) decay within ~2 weeks
observation: wordOfDay.ts rotates 8 entries by day-of-year, so the 'word of the day' repeats every 8 days — a returning user sees a duplicate inside a fortnight. playlists.ts offers 4 lists totalling ~12 short tracks. Both are well built and honest (counts are derived facts, deterministic rotation), but the volume is far below what a daily-return habit needs. These are exactly the surfaces meant to pull users back, and they run dry fastest.
recommendation: Expand word-of-day to at least 60-90 entries (a quarter of non-repeating dailies) and each playlist to 8-12 tracks. These are cheap, high-frequency retention touchpoints; at current volume the 'come back tomorrow' promise visibly breaks within two weeks.

Overall: the spec is strategically sound and honest about the persona-consistency stakes — one warm neural "Camille" voice everywhere is a genuine, high-leverage retention lever, and the accessibility/honesty rules (captions, "never fake a premium-voice indicator") are exactly right. But the spec is essentially a greenfield feature: 0% of it is built. Every one of the 17 corpus items has audioRef=null, the client never reaches the TTS edge function, and — most important — the flagship "podcast that pauses for you" guided-walkthrough has no data model behind it. The current Lesson is a flat list of typed sections (teach/table/examples/quiz…), not the "7 stages" with interaction points the spec narrates over; there is no segment/timestamp field, no pause-marker, no per-item slow-take slot, and no per-scenario-turn audio field. Several concrete promises in the spec are already false against the code (the player "timestamp concept" was deleted as fake; the pace picker is already real). The most urgent pedagogical risk is that the ONE track that actually has content (Sons/phonics) is taught by per-handset device TTS whose nasal/liaison/R rendering is unreliable — i.e. the app can actively teach wrong pronunciation. Recommend: (1) a schema extension for narration (segments, interaction points, multi-asset audio per item/turn) before any batch generation; (2) reconcile the voice-provider decision with what's wired; (3) prioritize real slow renders for Sons over everything else.
topic: Guided-walkthrough has no content schema behind it
observation: Spec §3 is the product's centerpiece — narration broken into addressable segments tied to 'content blocks/stages', karaoke highlight-in-sync, and a pause at each 'interaction point' ('Now you try'). None of this exists in the data model. The shipped Lesson (schema.ts) is a flat ordered list of 12 typed sections (teach/steps/table/examples/quiz/practice/audio…). There is no 'stage' concept (the spec keeps saying 'all 7 stages' — no 7-stage structure exists), no segment map field, no interaction-point / pause marker, and no per-segment audioRef. app/lesson.tsx renders sections then a quiz; there is nothing for a narration engine to synchronize to or pause on.
recommendation: Before writing any generation code, extend schema.ts: add an ordered segment/timestamp map ([{blockId,startMs,endMs,text}]) per narrated section and an explicit `interaction` marker type so the engine knows where to pause and wait. Treat the 'podcast that pauses for you' as a schema project first, an audio project second. Until the lesson unit can express interaction points, the guided-autoplay experience cannot be built as described.

topic: Device TTS teaches wrong pronunciation on the one track that has content
observation: Sons (phonics) is the most-built track (nasals ɔ̃/ɑ̃/ɛ̃/œ̃, mandatory liaison lé-zami, the French R). It is taught today by expo-speech fr-FR (tts.ts), which the spec itself calls robotic and per-handset. Device engines frequently mis-render exactly these features (denasalization, dropped/added liaison, uvular vs approximant R). A pronunciation course delivered by an unreliable voice doesn't just feel cheap — it can drill the wrong target sound into the learner.
recommendation: Invert the spec's build order: §4 flags 'real slow render for phonics/Sons/dictation' as a small special case, but it should be the FIRST fixed audio generated, not the exception. Human-verify every Sons/liaison/nasal clip before ship. Do not rely on time-stretch for these (see connected-speech note).

topic: Time-stretch cannot fake authentic connected speech at A2+
observation: Spec §4 resolves pace as 'one cached asset, time-stretch everywhere; a real slow render only for the pronunciation-critical few.' Time-stretching a slowly-enunciated clip to 1.25/1.5x does NOT reproduce the reductions, elisions and liaisons of natural fast French — the very features listening comprehension must train (métro announcements in the L'Oreille playlist, A2 'everyday situations'). Speeding up a careful clip yields a fast careful clip, not authentic speech.

Reserve pure time-stretch for convenience replays of already-natural audio. This is a CEFR-soundness issue: comprehension at A2/B1 depends on hearing connected speech, which a stretched slow master never contains.

topic: Fixed-audio corpus is 0% built and the schema can't hold what the spec needs
observation: All 17 audioRef values in seed.json are null; Item carries a single optional audioRef ('Null until Phase 7'). The spec needs MULTIPLE assets per unit that this one field cannot express: word pronunciation vs its example sentence (voiceflash), a natural take vs a real slow take (§4), and per-roleplay-turn audio (ScenarioTurn is {ai,en,user} with no audio field at all). topic: Voice-provider decision contradicts what is actually wired
observation: Resolved Decision A picks an fr-FR neural baseline from Azure / OpenAI / Google / Polly and says 'ElevenLabs not needed for launch.' topic: Narration is not tied into the existing spaced-repetition loop
observation: A real SM-2 scheduler already exists (progress.logic.ts: srsCards/dueCards, ease 1.3–3.0, 1→3→interval×ease ladder) and feeds app/review + smartreview. topic: Curriculum spine mismatch — plan's unit lists vs shipped curriculum.ts / seed.json
observation: The plan's §3 unit lists were carried over from the old pre-Phase-1 curriculum doc and diverge from the spine the app actually renders and the seed encodes. Sons: plan lists 'Le e (muet/fermé/ouvert)', 'semi-voyelles (oi·ui·-ille)', 'liaisons', 'accent tonique & rythme du groupe'; curriculum.ts/seed ship sons.01–09 as alphabet, voyelles, nasales, consonnes, accents, lettres muettes, élision, rythme, masterclass. Neither is a superset. A1: plan's 'lessons 1–4' = salutations, se présenter, nombres & l'heure, être & avoir; the shipped A1 spine puts genre (a1.03) and articles définis (a1.04) at positions 3–4, splits être (a1.06) and avoir (a1.07), and 'se présenter' is not a unit at all — and the ONLY A1 lesson already wired (a1.04.l1 'Les articles définis') is absent from the plan's A1 1–4. A2: plan's 1–4 = passé composé avoir, passé composé être, pronoms objets, futur proche; curriculum.ts a2.01–04 = verbes réguliers, irréguliers, adjectifs & adverbes, prépositions, with passé composé/futur proche/reflexives all buried under a2.05 in a2Subs. recommendation: Before any generation, reconcile §3 against curriculum.ts/seed.json and pick ONE canonical unit spine (recommend the shipped one, since the Den renders it and ids are immutable). Rewrite the Sons/A1/A2 lesson targets as concrete unit ids (sons.01…, a1.01…, a2.01…) so generated lessonIds slot into existing units. Make the wired a1.04 'articles définis' and a2.01 'verbes réguliers' part of the A1/A2 deep set explicitly. Derive the level-discipline vocab whitelist from that same canonical order.

topic: The lesson→corpus join (practice sections / itemIds) is the retention engine and the plan omits it
observation: schema.ts's whole thesis is that a Lesson exercises four skills by referencing corpus items via `practice` sections and `itemIds`, and that the SRS/Smart Review grow from attempts logged against those item ids. But all three shipped lessons have itemIds: [] and zero practice sections, so the lesson→drill join is currently DEAD, and the plan's rich-lesson spec (§3a 'teach → examples → minimal pairs → common errors → cheat sheet → quiz') never mentions practice sections or itemIds. progress.logic.ts confirms the SRS only schedules SCHEDULABLE drill activities (flashcards, voiceflash, dictation, sentence, review) — lesson/roleplay/speak are explicitly excluded. Make 'lesson has ≥1 practice section with resolvable itemIds' a machine-gate rule. This is what converts lesson study into review-deck cards.

## Ealch v2 content review: contentresearch.md vs. what the app actually produces

**Scope reviewed:** contentresearch.md (full, 1749 lines) against ealch-v2/src/content/ (schema.ts, curriculum.ts, lessons.ts, drills.ts, playlists.ts, wordOfDay.ts, index.ts, seed.json), ealch-v2/src/services/ (content.ts, content.logic.ts, tts.ts), and the retention-critical logic in ealch-v2/src/store/progress.logic.ts and schema.sql.

### Headline
The document itself is an unusually strong pedagogy/retention review — its diagnoses (perception-before-production, register as function not colour, never a bare noun, SRS as the spine, "no on-screen number that is not a fold over the logs") are correct and specific. The problem is not the document; it is that **the codebase has since moved past the document's snapshot in a way that skipped the one decision the document flagged as time-boxed.**

The doc (dated 2026-07-14) asserts "0 Items in corpus," "the SRS does not exist," and "0 files import schema.ts." All three are now **stale**: seed.json carries 17 items / 3 lessons / 2 scenarios / 17 units, the app loads it through a real ContentService (content.ts), and progress.logic.ts now implements an attempt log (`AttemptEntry`) plus a working day-granular scheduler (`srsCards`/`dueCards`/`reviewDueCount`). So Phases 0/2/3/4 of the doc's plan are substantially done.

**But Phase 1 — "amend the schema, before any authoring" — was not done, and content was authored against the old 12-type schema anyway.** schema.ts is unchanged: still 12 section types, `useCases` still has no `register`, `quiz` still has no `itemId`, `table` still has no audio, and none of `paradigm`/`minimalPair`/`story`/`recall`/`practice.mode` exist. The seed lessons use only 6 basic section types (table, examples, audio, commonErrors, quiz, focus). The document's central warning — "every breaking schema change is free today and expensive in three weeks" — has now partly triggered: there is live content to migrate, and the SRS has been built on a shape (item-only key, SM-2, no modality) that the doc argued at length against.

### CEFR / level soundness
- Curriculum sequencing is still exactly as the doc criticised: negation is unit 18 of 26 and questions are units 19–20 (curriculum.ts:48–50), so a learner cannot ask or deny anything for two-thirds of A1. `on` is still absent from the subject-pronoun unit (curriculum.ts:35). There are still no CEFR can-do statements anywhere — `Unit` is `{title, sub}` (curriculum.ts:5), so there is no assessment anchor and the track reads as a grammar-topic list ("Le genre des noms") rather than functions.
- Phonics allocation is still backwards by communicative cost: "consonant sounds & the French r" gets its own unit (curriculum.ts:22) while all oral vowels are crammed into one (curriculum.ts:20), and there is no /y/–/u/ unit at all. The nasal lesson (lessons.ts / seed sons.03.l1) teaches four distinct nasals including /œ̃/, which has largely merged with /ɛ̃/ in modern standard French — a low-value contrast taught as if high-value.
- The nasal lesson jumps straight to production with no discrimination/perception step, exactly as the doc's §2.8 says. There is no `minimalPair` type and no discriminate-to-criterion mode anywhere in the corpus.

### Retention / motivation
- Honesty discipline is genuinely good and worth preserving: streaks are a fold over a real session log, playlists carry real French with derived counts (playlists.ts), and word-of-day is a deterministic rotation. This is the codebase's strongest asset.
- But word-of-day content is C1/C2 literary abstract nouns (flânerie, dépaysement, émerveillement, insouciance) shown to A1 beginners — aspirational and beautiful, but not vocabulary a beginner can use or retain. It trains admiration, not acquisition.
- The article-detachment problem persists: `sbWords` still splits `un` and `café` into separate bubbles (index.ts:45–51), teaching that the determiner is optional — the opposite of "never a bare noun."

### Spaced-repetition / review-loop fit
- The SRS is real and derived (good), but it is **SM-2 keyed on `itemId` only** — no `modality`, so "I recognise la gare" and "I can say la gare" are one card. In a voice-first app this is the exact failure the doc's §5.4 spends the most words on: the easy recognition memory masks the hard production one.
- There is no retrievability and no mastery gate. The honest "mastered" signal the doc wants (`reps>=3 ∧ R>=0.90`) does not exist; the closest proxy is `itemsPracticed` = "≥1 correct attempt ever" (progress.logic.ts:276), which is "met," not "retained." SM-2's miss handling resets `reps` and interval to 0 (applyGrade grade 0), the reset-to-zero the doc calls hostile for language items.
- `dueCards`/`reviewDueCount` have no daily cap — a returning learner after two weeks gets the full backlog, the single biggest SRS churn event the doc names.
- The lesson quiz cannot feed the SRS: `QuizQ` has no `itemId` (schema.ts:186), so quiz misses only reach the weak-spot ErrorEvent log via the coarse `lessonSkill` map (curriculum.ts:13). Attempts are logged only from dictation/flashcards/review/roleplay/sentence.

### Script / narration / examiner quality
- All audio is still device TTS: the remote-provider branch in tts.ts:38–41 is a no-op comment, exactly as the doc's §6.3 says. "Slow" is client-side rate 0.7 (tts.ts:74) — below the doc's 0.75 floor and pitch-shifting a rate change, which alters French vowels.
- The pronunciation signal is still an ASR text-match verdict (`AttemptEntry.verdict` good/close/off from `heard` transcript), structurally blind to the /y/–/u/ and nasal contrasts the app's flagship lesson teaches.
- "Examiner": placement is a single question (drills.ts:11) and the level then defaults to `'B1'` (useStore.ts:139) — a CEFR claim on ~zero evidence, mirrored server-side (schema.sql:32).

### Document-vs-code fidelity
- Server schema.sql still carries every §8.1 liability the doc listed: `level default 'B1'` (:32), `streak int default 0` (:36), `review_items` with denormalised content and FSRS-init column defaults and no `last_review_at`/`reps`/`lapses` (:41–50), and no `attempts` table at all. The client went derived-and-honest; the server did not follow.
- Net: the app implemented the plumbing (corpus + attempt log + scheduler) but skipped the schema amendment and the modality/FSRS/mastery decisions that were the doc's actual point. The reviewers should re-baseline the document against HEAD before acting on it — several of its most quoted facts are now false, while its recommendations (register, modality, perception-first, mastery signal, server cleanup) remain unbuilt and are now migrations rather than free changes.
topic: SRS keys on item only, not (item, modality)
observation: progress.logic.ts srsCards()/AttemptEntry have no modality field; recognise (fr→en) and produce (en→fr/say) fold into one SM-2 card per itemId. In a voice-first app the easy recognition memory masks the hard production memory, so the scheduler under-drills exactly the skill that is the product.
recommendation: Add modality ('recognise'|'produce'|'discriminate') to AttemptEntry and key srsCards on (itemId, modality). Gate the produce card behind recognise reaching a stability floor (doc §5.4 sibling-gating) so review load does not triple on day one.
